# The real measurements of Gorman et al. 2014, as packaged by palmerpenguins.
main <- function(inputs, report, run) {
  outputs <- list()
  p <- palmerpenguins::penguins
  p <- p[complete.cases(p[, c("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm")]), ]
  file <- file.path(run$output_directory, "penguins.csv")
  write.csv(p[, c("species", "sex", "island", "bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm")], file, row.names = FALSE)
  outputs[["penguins"]] <- list(value = file)
  counts <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(p$species, p$island))
  counts <- cbind(Species = rownames(counts), counts, Total = rowSums(counts))
  report$log(paste0(nrow(p), " penguins with both bill measurements"))
  report$table(counts)

  outputs
}

# Pearson's r of bill length and bill depth: overall and within each stratum.
main <- function(inputs, report, run) {
  outputs <- list()
  by <- inputs$params$stratify
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("penguins"))
  if (!by %in% c("species", "sex", "island")) stop("stratify must be species, sex or island, not ", by)
  d$stratum <- d[[by]]
  d <- d[!is.na(d$stratum), ]  # sex is unknown for some penguins

  line <- function(name, x) {
    test <- cor.test(x$bill_length_mm, x$bill_depth_mm)
    data.frame(stratify = by, stratum = name, n = nrow(x), r = unname(test$estimate),
               lower = test$conf.int[1], upper = test$conf.int[2],
               slope = unname(coef(lm(bill_depth_mm ~ bill_length_mm, x))[2]))
  }
  overall <- line("All", d)
  strata <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$stratum), function(x) line(x$stratum[1], x)))
  result <- rbind(overall, strata)
  result$reversed <- sign(result$r) != sign(overall$r)

  points <- file.path(run$output_directory, "points.csv")
  write.csv(d[, c("stratum", "bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm")], points, row.names = FALSE)
  correlations <- file.path(run$output_directory, "correlations.csv")
  write.csv(result, correlations, row.names = FALSE)
  outputs[["points"]] <- list(value = points)
  outputs[["correlations"]] <- list(value = correlations)

  shown <- data.frame(
    Stratum = result$stratum, n = result$n, r = sprintf("%.3f", result$r),
    `95%CI` = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", result$lower, result$upper),
    Slope = sprintf("%.3f", result$slope),
    Direction = ifelse(result$stratum == "All", "", ifelse(result$reversed, "opposite to all", "same as all")),
    check.names = FALSE)
  report$table(shown)

  outputs
}

library(ggplot2)

# The same points with the overall line and one line per stratum.
main <- function(inputs, report) {
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("points"))
  r <- read.csv(inputs$path("correlations"))
  strata <- r[r$stratum != "All", ]
  labels <- setNames(sprintf("%s (r = %.2f)", strata$stratum, strata$r), strata$stratum)
  figure <- ggplot(d, aes(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = stratum), alpha = 0.55, size = 1.4) +
    geom_smooth(aes(colour = stratum), method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#009E73")[seq_len(nrow(strata))], labels = labels, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)",
         title = sprintf("Stratified by %s: all (dashed) r = %.2f", r$stratify[1], r$r[r$stratum == "All"])) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  report$figure(print(figure), alt = "Bill length against bill depth, overall and by stratum", width = 7.5, height = 5.2)

  invisible(NULL)
}

cards.summary: Compare the three stratifications side by side
details: Compare the three stratifications side by side

files.text:
library(ggplot2)

# r per stratum for all three stratifying variables, side by side.
main <- function(inputs, report) {
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("penguins"))
  overall <- cor(d$bill_length_mm, d$bill_depth_mm)
  rows <- lapply(c("species", "sex", "island"), function(by) {
    x <- d[!is.na(d[[by]]), ]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(split(x, x[[by]]), function(s) {
      test <- cor.test(s$bill_length_mm, s$bill_depth_mm)
      data.frame(by = by, stratum = s[[by]][1], n = nrow(s), r = unname(test$estimate),
                 lower = test$conf.int[1], upper = test$conf.int[2])
    }))
  })
  rows <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rows$by <- factor(rows$by, levels = c("species", "sex", "island"))
  rows$side <- ifelse(sign(rows$r) != sign(overall), "opposite to all", "same direction as all")
  rows$label <- sprintf("%s (n=%d)", rows$stratum, rows$n)
  verdict <- tapply(rows$side == "opposite to all", rows$by, sum)
  report$log(paste0("strata reversed: ", paste(names(verdict), verdict, collapse = ", ")))
  figure <- ggplot(rows, aes(r, reorder(label, r), colour = side)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = overall, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0, orientation = "y", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 2.8) +
    facet_grid(by ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("opposite to all" = "#D55E00", "same direction as all" = "#0072B2"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Pearson's r (lines are 95% confidence intervals)", y = NULL,
         title = sprintf("Whether it reverses depends on the stratifying variable: the dashed line is all, r = %.2f", overall)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  report$figure(print(figure), alt = "Correlation in each stratum for species, sex and island", width = 7.5, height = 5.2)

  invisible(NULL)
}

# UCBAdmissions from base R's datasets: Berkeley, autumn 1973.
main <- function(inputs, report, run) {
  outputs <- list()
  t <- datasets::UCBAdmissions
  rows <- as.data.frame(t, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(rows) <- c("admit", "gender", "dept", "count")
  file <- file.path(run$output_directory, "admissions.csv")
  write.csv(rows, file, row.names = FALSE)
  outputs[["admissions"]] <- list(value = file)

  or <- function(m) m["Admitted", "Male"] * m["Rejected", "Female"] / (m["Rejected", "Male"] * m["Admitted", "Female"])
  line <- function(name, m) data.frame(
    Department = name,
    `Male applicants` = sum(m[, "Male"]), `Male admit rate` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * m["Admitted", "Male"] / sum(m[, "Male"])),
    `Female applicants` = sum(m[, "Female"]), `Female admit rate` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * m["Admitted", "Female"] / sum(m[, "Female"])),
    `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.2f", or(m)))
  by_dept <- do.call(rbind, lapply(dimnames(t)$Dept, function(k) line(k, t[, , k])))
  all <- line("All (aggregated)", margin.table(t, c(1, 2)))
  mh <- mantelhaen.test(t, correct = FALSE)
  common <- data.frame(Department = "Adjusted for department (Mantel–Haenszel)", `Male applicants` = "", `Male admit rate` = "", `Female applicants` = "", `Female admit rate` = "",
                       `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", mh$estimate, mh$conf.int[1], mh$conf.int[2]))
  report$log(paste0(sprintf("Mantel-Haenszel common odds ratio %.4f, X2 %.3f, p %.3f", mh$estimate, mh$statistic, mh$p.value)))
  report$table(rbind(by_dept, all, common))

  outputs
}

library(ggplot2)

# Why the totals differ: rates by department, drawn by where people applied.
main <- function(inputs, report) {
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("admissions"))
  wide <- aggregate(count ~ gender + dept, d, sum)
  names(wide)[3] <- "applied"
  admitted <- d[d$admit == "Admitted", c("gender", "dept", "count")]
  wide <- merge(wide, admitted)
  wide$rate <- 100 * wide$count / wide$applied
  overall <- aggregate(cbind(count, applied) ~ gender, wide, sum)
  overall$rate <- 100 * overall$count / overall$applied
  wide$gender <- factor(wide$gender, c("Male", "Female"), c("Men", "Women"))
  overall$gender <- factor(overall$gender, c("Male", "Female"), c("Men", "Women"))
  colours <- c("Men" = "#0072B2", "Women" = "#D55E00")
  figure <- ggplot(wide, aes(dept, rate, colour = gender)) +
    geom_hline(data = overall, aes(yintercept = rate, colour = gender), linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_text(data = overall, aes(x = 6.45, y = rate, label = sprintf("All %s %.1f%%", gender, rate)),
              hjust = 1, vjust = -0.5, size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(aes(size = applied), alpha = 0.75, position = position_dodge(width = 0.35)) +
    scale_x_discrete() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours, name = NULL) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 13, name = "Applicants") +
    labs(x = "Department (anonymised A–F)", y = "Admission rate (%)", title = "Women's applications leaned towards departments with low admission rates") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  report$figure(print(figure), alt = "Admission rate by department and gender, with the number of applicants", width = 7.5, height = 5.2)

  invisible(NULL)
}

notes.html:
A relationship that reverses between the aggregate and the strata

A correlation or a ratio can change even its sign depending on whether the data is seen together or split into strata (Simpson's paradox). The overall correlation is the sum of the correlation within strata and the differences between them.

Cov⁡(X,Y)=E[Cov⁡(X,Y∣Z)]⏟within strata+Cov⁡(E[X∣Z], E[Y∣Z])⏟between strata\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y) = \underbrace{\mathrm{E}[\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y \mid Z)]}_{\text{within strata}} + \underbrace{\operatorname{Cov}(\mathrm{E}[X \mid Z],\, \mathrm{E}[Y \mid Z])}_{\text{between strata}}

Upper branch: Palmer Penguins (Gorman, Williams & Fraser 2014, measured at Palmer Station, Antarctica; the palmerpenguins package). The correlation of bill length and depth. Change stratify of correlate to species / sex / island and rerun from there. survey shows the three side by side. By species it reverses in every stratum, by sex it does not, and by island only Biscoe (where Adélie and Gentoo mix) stays negative.

Lower branch: applications to Berkeley's graduate school in 1973 (Bickel, Hammel & O'Connell 1975; R's UCBAdmissions). Overall, men were admitted more readily; adjusted for department, the difference almost disappears.

Stratifying is not always right. Which to read is decided by the causal question. If the choice of department arises as a consequence of sex (mediation), you must not adjust for department when asking about "the total effect of sex". If the question is whether each department's review discriminated, stratifying gets closer to the answer. Even then, an unmeasured confounder remains: differences among applicants within a department. The data alone cannot tell these apart; the question has to be decided before reading the values.
